2. **A refresh that a crash cut short is finished, never redone, and an owner's value is still never taken for Google's (#108 item 68).** When a field Google changed since the stored sidecar JSON already holds Google's new value in the sidecar (the process died after `xmp.refresh` wrote it and before `stage_place` committed), `xmp.applied` counts it as refreshed: nothing is written again, the stored JSON is advanced, `metadata_refreshed` is recorded and the person's library is rescanned. The conditions are those of `xmp.changes` (Google changed it, the file itself carries none) with the sidecar equal to the new value instead of the old one, so a sidecar holding any other value is left alone. Held by `tests/test_incremental.py` (`test_a_refresh_killed_after_the_sidecar_was_written_is_finished_by_the_retry`; negative: `test_a_sidecar_the_owner_set_to_another_value_is_still_not_refreshed_on_a_retry`, `test_a_description_the_owner_edited_since_is_not_overwritten`) and `tests/test_xmp.py` (`test_a_sidecar_already_holding_googles_new_values_counts_them_as_applied`, `test_nothing_counts_as_applied_unless_google_changed_it_and_the_sidecar_holds_the_new_value`).
3. **A refreshed location is the item's location too (#108 item 69).** When a refresh writes or finds Google's new location in the sidecar, the `MediaItem`'s `lat`, `lon` and `gps_source` (`google`) are set to it in the same commit, so `review.missing_gps` stops listing it; a location the refresh refused (the owner's, or the file's own) changes nothing. Held by `tests/test_incremental.py` (`test_a_location_google_adds_later_is_stored_on_the_item_and_leaves_missing_gps`; negative: `test_a_location_the_owner_already_set_keeps_the_item_missing_gps_when_google_adds_one`).
4. **A link or a folder at the sidecar's place is never written through, and counts as skipped (#108 item 70).** `place.refresh_takeout` checks the sidecar's place with `paths.checked_sidecar` before the refresh reads or writes anything, and on `paths.NotASidecar` counts the item as skipped, as it does a link at the photo or a folder on the way: the photo is already in the library, so the run's `failed` count (which keeps staging from cleanup) is not raised. Nothing outside is changed, the stored JSON stays as it was and no `metadata_refreshed` is recorded. Held by `tests/test_incremental.py` (`test_a_link_at_the_sidecar_is_skipped_and_never_written_through`, `test_a_folder_at_the_sidecar_is_skipped_and_left_alone`).
5. **The stored Google JSON is advanced field by field, and keeps the old value of a field Google removed (#108 item 71).** After every refresh that read the photo and sidecar, written or not, `MediaItem.sidecar_json` becomes `xmp.baseline(old, new)`: the new export's JSON, except that for a description or location Google removed (`xmp.removes`) the old record's value is kept; a new export whose JSON for the photo is missing, does not parse or is not an object keeps the old record whole, and with no usable old record the new JSON is taken as it is. So an owner's edit, a date-only change and a field the refresh wrote or found applied all move to Google's current value, while a removed value, which the sidecar still holds, stays the baseline: a value Google sets again later, alone or in the same export as a change to the other field, still matches what Darkroom wrote and reaches the sidecar and the item. A photo or sidecar that cannot be read, or a refusal before reading (a link, a path outside google-only), keeps the stored JSON too. A sidecar write that fails after the checks (`paths.write_sidecar` raising, including its `NotASidecar` when no file was written) is a failed item, not a skip. Held by `tests/test_incremental.py` (`test_a_refresh_with_nothing_to_write_advances_the_stored_google_record_and_leaves_the_sidecar`, `test_a_value_google_removed_and_later_set_again_still_reaches_the_sidecar`, `test_a_location_google_removed_while_changing_the_description_is_refreshed_when_google_adds_a_new_one`, `test_a_description_google_removed_while_moving_the_photo_is_refreshed_when_google_sets_it_again`, `test_an_owner_edited_description_beside_a_refreshed_location_keeps_the_edit_and_advances_both_fields`, `test_an_export_without_the_photos_json_keeps_the_stored_record_for_the_next_re_add`, `test_a_sidecar_write_that_fails_after_the_check_is_a_failed_item_not_a_skip`; negative: `test_a_refresh_that_cannot_read_the_photo_keeps_the_stored_record_and_logs_nothing` and the linked-folder, linked-file and outside-folder tests) and `tests/test_xmp.py` (`test_a_value_google_dropped_counts_as_removed_and_a_change_does_not`, `test_the_baseline_takes_googles_new_values_and_keeps_the_old_one_only_for_a_removed_field`, `test_every_shape_of_a_later_record_keeps_a_removed_value_for_the_next_re_add`).

## Resolving Takeout copies (#234)

Filled in by #234's pull requests. The owner's decision of Nov 7 (#234, #199), in full: "Let's make sure we're not storing duplicate images permanently - figure out which one is higher quality and keep that one. If both images are identical, get rid of the duplicate." On how the duplicate goes (#234): "if a duplicate exists on Unraid, delete the duplicate", with no trash area. This supersedes "dedupe deletes nothing on Unraid" for the losing copy of a matched pair only, never anything else. Items 1 and 2 come with the remover (#244, #247); items 3 to 7 are appended by #238 with the caller.

1. **Only the losing copy of a matched pair is deleted, and only through one remover.** A matched pair is a Takeout copy in a person's `google-only/` and an Immich original of the same person in `originals/immich/` that are the same photo by an automatic tier 1 or 2 match; the loser is the Takeout copy unless the Takeout copy has strictly more pixels. Only `paths.remove_losing_copy` deletes it, with its `.xmp`, and nothing else; Semgrep's `darkroom-losing-copy-one-caller` allows one caller module, `darkroom/domain/takeout_copies.py` (item 3). Held by `darkroom-losing-copy-one-caller` (examples in `.semgrep/examples/darkroom/domain/losing_copy.py`).
2. **The keeper is checked before anything goes.** `remove_losing_copy` refuses a loser outside `<person>/google-only/` or `<person>/originals/immich/`, a keeper outside the same person's `google-only/` or `originals/`, a link anywhere on the way (each folder opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` from the photo root), a folder, a keeper that is missing or not the SHA-1 Darkroom recorded, a loser that is not the SHA-1 Darkroom recorded, and a keeper and loser that are the same file (hard link). The keeper must have one link; it is held open with its folder pinned, and a private `.keeping-<random>` hard link to it is kept until the loser is gone and is put back at the keeper's name (never deleted) if that name no longer points at it, so a keeper swapped at any step still leaves a copy. The loser is claimed with `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` (or, where that is not supported, a link whose inode is checked against the name again right before the name is unlinked) to a bounded name in its pinned folder, so nothing is ever replaced and a 255-byte name still works. The claimed inode and SHA-1 are checked and the keeper re-checked before the claim is unlinked, and only if the claim is still that inode. The claim is the file `copy` inside a private folder (`.losing-<sha1 prefix>-<name hash>/`, mode 0700, owned by Darkroom's user, refused otherwise), so the final unlink acts on a name in a folder only Darkroom's user can change, and only after the claimed entry is checked to be the inode that was hashed (a file swapped in there survives). The keeper's sidecar is published with `renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE)` and the old one is checked after the exchange and swapped back if another writer changed it (refused where exchange is unsupported, never a plain replace; a temp file is removed only while it holds our data or the old sidecar, so a newer sidecar caught in a race is left on disk rather than lost). If the keeper's name is taken while it is held and the held link can't go back, the removal raises, so the caller never records it as clean, and the photo stays under its `.keeping-` name, which recovery never removes because it no longer links the file at the keeper's name (`test_a_keeper_whose_name_is_taken_after_the_loser_went_is_kept_and_reported`). A removal takes an exclusive `flock` on the keeper while it holds it, so a second removal sharing that keeper is refused instead of taking the first one's live `.keeping-` link for debris. A `.keeping-<16 hex>` link a hard crash left (its lock died with the process) is removed once it is proved to link the keeper; any other name, even one starting with `.keeping-`, is never touched. The private claim folder is locked with `flock` while a removal uses it, and a busy keeper or claim refuses without restoring anything, so one removal never undoes another's active claim. `restore_losing_copy` puts back only a regular file with the recorded SHA-1 and reports success only if that same inode is at the name afterwards. The sidecar is written in full (short writes are looped) before it is published, and the rollback after a changed old sidecar happens only while the name still holds our data, and is undone again if a newer sidecar came in meanwhile. The loser's sidecar is put back, not removed, if a photo is at the loser's name again by the time it is claimed. An interrupted link fallback that left the loser at both its name and the claim is finished by removing both links of that inode. Held by `RemoveLosingCopyTests` (`test_a_keeper_link_left_by_a_hard_crash_is_recovered`, `test_a_link_fallback_cut_short_between_link_and_unlink_is_finished`, `test_a_file_swapped_into_the_private_claim_folder_before_the_unlink_survives`, `test_a_claim_folder_that_is_not_darkroom_private_is_refused`, `test_a_newer_sidecar_written_while_the_keepers_was_staged_is_never_discarded`, `test_a_keeper_link_held_by_a_removal_in_progress_is_never_taken_for_crash_debris`, `test_a_sidecar_rollback_never_discards_a_newer_sidecar`, `test_a_short_write_never_publishes_a_truncated_sidecar`, `test_a_new_photo_and_sidecar_at_the_name_keep_their_sidecar`). A failed check puts the claim back without replacing anything. A claim left by a crash is finished by the next call for the pair, or put back by `restore_losing_copy` when the removal is refused, so it never hides a file for good. The loser's `.xmp` is removed only once nothing is at the photo's name, by the same claim and inode check. `Keeper.sidecar`/`Keeper.write_sidecar` are a second sidecar writer, needed because the keeper's sidecar must be written through its pinned folder rather than a path that could have been swapped for a link. It refuses an old sidecar that changed, a sidecar that is a link and a keeper that is no longer the recorded file. Held by `tests/test_paths.py`'s `RemoveLosingCopyTests` (a file swapped in for the loser or keeper at every step, a file put at the claim name, a swapped sidecar, a crash between claim and unlink and at the sidecar claim, a 250-byte name, the link fallback and a swap during it, and the sidecar writer's positives and negatives). The remover's internals (`drop_losing_copy`, `restore_losing_copy`, `checked_keeper`) are held to the same one caller by `darkroom-losing-copy-one-caller`. A crash while claiming the loser's sidecar leaves a `.losing-…xmp` claim that the next call removes once the photo is gone.
3. **The caller pairs only what qualifies (appended by #238).** Every Takeout copy placed in the person's `google-only/`, eligible or not, is in the dedupe input as a peer, here and in `finish`'s re-run, so an owner-made, reversed or reviewed copy of the same shot keeps the match ambiguous; only the resulting decisions for eligible copies may become pairs (`test_an_ineligible_takeout_peer_of_the_same_shot_keeps_the_match_ambiguous`, `test_an_ineligible_peer_that_appears_after_the_removal_is_recorded_refuses_it`). A pair is a Takeout item of one person in that person's `google-only/` and a phone original the Immich reconcile stored for that person in `originals/immich/` (known from its `immich_assets` row, not its path), matched by `dedupe.decide_all` at tier 1 (same SHA-1) or tier 2 (unique on both sides; an ambiguous shot, tier 3 or 4 never pair). Every decision that names the Takeout item must be an unreversed automatic tier 5 for that person, and none may be owner-made, reversed, kept-both, tier 1 to 4 or for an edited copy, and no decision of any kind may name it as its match (a later export's tier 1 match, for example); edited is read from the decision's recorded export path, not from the library name, which a name collision can change. Rebuilt candidates carry that edited flag too, so an edited variant of the same shot is never counted as a rival (`test_an_edited_variant_of_the_same_shot_is_not_a_rival_of_its_original`). Another person's file and an original outside `originals/immich/` never pair. `darkroom/domain/takeout_copies.py` is the one caller of `paths.remove_losing_copy`. Held by Semgrep's `darkroom-losing-copy-one-caller` and `tests/test_takeout_copies.py` (`test_an_original_the_reconcile_did_not_store_never_pairs`, `test_a_copy_with_any_doubtful_decision_never_pairs_even_beside_a_later_tier_five`, `test_an_edited_copy_renamed_on_a_name_collision_never_pairs`, `test_ambiguous_and_review_level_matches_remove_nothing`, `test_another_persons_copies_are_never_paired`).
4. **Only more pixels make a phone original lose.** The reconcile offers its stored originals to the Pixels only after resolving duplicates, and does both even when a later asset fails the run, so nothing removed is offered and nothing stored is kept from the Pixel (`SettleTests`). Identical copies keep the phone original. Otherwise the Takeout copy wins only with strictly more pixels (width times height, and only when the phone original's are known); at equal resolution the phone original stays whatever the file size or metadata. A phone original loses only while nothing depends on it: no dedupe decision matches it, no Pixel copy of it was placed or pruned, it is not `confirmed_in_google`, its Takeout copy's export still exists and every Pixel of the person uploads to that export's account (so that account already has the better copy); otherwise both stay. A removed phone original's queued Pixel copies go with its row and it is not sent to a Pixel; a kept one is sent as before (decision 5), keeps its flag and decisions, and only phone items carry `confirmed_in_google`, so removing a Takeout copy loses no confirmation. Held by `tests/test_takeout_copies.py` (`QualityRuleTests`, including a same-resolution bigger Takeout file that never deletes the phone original, `test_a_takeout_copy_with_more_pixels_beats_the_phone_original_which_is_not_sent_to_the_pixel`, `test_the_phone_original_stays_while_anything_depends_on_it_even_when_that_appears_after_the_removal_is_recorded`, a negative for each dependency, before and after the removal is recorded) and `tests/test_immich_reconcile.py`'s `TakeoutCopyTests`.
5. **Google's metadata survives the Takeout copy.** The carry runs inside the remover's single keeper lock (`remove_losing_copy`'s `carry` step), and the exact sidecar bytes the carry verified (or the sidecar it found already complete) are compared with the kept copy's sidecar right before the loser's claim is unlinked; any change, including a replacement right after the carry published, keeps the loser (`test_a_sidecar_replaced_right_after_the_carry_published_it_keeps_the_loser`) (`test_a_keeper_sidecar_changed_after_the_carry_keeps_the_loser`). Before a Takeout copy goes, its stored Google JSON fills the kept original's sidecar through `xmp.fill` and `exiftool.write_xmp` (location and description, gaps only, never over a value the original or its sidecar has, as placing invariant 5 does for a tier 1 or 2 match), and a re-read must show no gap left; a write that fails or can't be verified refuses the removal and both copies stay. When the phone original is the loser, the kept Takeout copy keeps its own sidecar and nothing is carried. Held by `tests/test_takeout_copies.py` (`test_an_identical_takeout_copy_leaves_and_its_google_metadata_moves_to_the_originals_sidecar`, `test_a_value_the_keeper_already_has_is_kept`, `test_a_sidecar_that_cannot_be_written_refuses_and_removes_nothing`) and `TakeoutCopyTests` with the real exiftool.
6. **A crash, a failed check or a change in between never leaves zero copies, and nothing is redone.** A pending removal whose loser is already gone (a crash after the unlink, before the record) is finished as removed through the remover, which still checks the keeper; it is never marked refused while it points at a deleted file or while its loser sits hidden in its claim (a row is refused only once nothing is claimed and the loser is back at its name), a busy keeper or claim leaves it pending to be retried (`test_a_loser_hidden_in_its_claim_is_never_marked_refused`, `test_a_busy_keeper_leaves_the_removal_pending_for_the_next_run`), and if the keeper doesn't check out it stays pending with a `duplicate_removal_failed` event (`test_a_crash_after_the_unlink_is_recorded_as_removed_even_when_a_check_now_fails`, `test_a_gone_loser_whose_records_changed_is_never_marked_refused`). Each removal is committed to `duplicate_removals` (migration 0024) as `pending` before anything is written or deleted. Finishing one (right away or on the next run) first takes SQLite's write lock, then re-checks the records, that the pair still qualifies (item 1; only this pair's Takeout decisions and Immich row, so the work under the lock doesn't grow with the library, `test_finishing_a_removal_queries_the_same_however_many_other_google_only_items_there_are`) and, for a phone loser, every dependency in item 3; anything changed marks it `refused` with one `duplicate_removal_refused` event and both copies stay, and a refused pair is never tried again. A loser or its folder already gone is finished once the keeper checks out. A filesystem error records a `duplicate_removal_failed` event and leaves it pending for the next run. The `immich_reconciled` event and log line count removed, refused and failed removals. A `removed` Takeout copy is never placed again by a retried import of any export whose decision named it (`run.stage_place`; one `removed` row per such decision). Each deletion is one `duplicate_removed` event naming the person, the copy's source, the rule and the tier, never a file name. Re-running changes nothing. Held by `tests/test_takeout_copies.py`'s `CrashTests`, the dependency test in item 3 and the identical-copy test (a second run changes nothing), and `tests/test_immich_reconcile.py`'s `TakeoutCopyTests` (a second reconcile and a retried import change no file).
7. **`dedupe.py` still deletes nothing.** The removal lives in its own module; `tests/test_dedupe_invariants.py`'s AST check now also refuses `remove_losing_copy`, `resolve_person`, `finish` and any reference to `takeout_copies` in `dedupe.py`.
